The review step feels like the right trade-off. I’d rather briefly confirm the fetched title and description than save misleading details. The list layout also feels readable, and the icon, description, address, and preview give me enough context. When organising is added, I’d expect each item’s tags to be visible here too.

The duplicate behaviour needs one adjustment: the host name can ignore capitalisation, and a harmless trailing slash is fine to ignore, but the rest of the address shouldn’t be lowercased. Paths and query details can point to different pages. I also wouldn’t automatically treat `http` and `https`, or `www` and a non-`www` address, as identical because they can differ. Warn me only when the safely normalised address really matches.

Editing the title and description later works as I’d expect. I’ll also need to be able to correct the saved address itself from that editor.
